title: Two Sum
statement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in increasing order.
hints: A nested pair scan is correct and quadratic. A dictionary turns the complement lookup into expected constant time.
Scan left to right. For the current value x, the partner you need is target minus x.
Store value to index as you go, and only look backward so an element is never paired with itself.

approaches.name: Hash map one pass
approaches.explanation: Map each seen value to its index and probe the complement.

editorial: The quadratic solution enumerates pairs. The linear solution remembers every value already seen. When nums[i] arrives, the complement target - nums[i] is either already in the map, in which case the pair is done, or it is recorded for a later index. Because a solution exists, the function always returns inside the loop.
